channel.title: Tanooki Auth blog
channel.description: Plain-English security tips from Tanooki Auth.

item.title: What two-factor authentication is, in plain English
item.description: Two-factor authentication means a stolen password alone can’t get someone into your account. Here’s how it works and which kind to pick.

item.title: Authenticator app codes vs text message codes
item.description: Text message codes are better than nothing, but authenticator app codes avoid SIM swaps and phone-network attacks. Here’s what the experts say.

item.title: What to do if you lose your phone
item.description: Lost or stolen phone? Lock it, protect your accounts, and get your two-factor codes back. A calm checklist with links to Apple and Google’s own steps.

item.title: Recovery codes: the spare key you’ll be glad you kept
item.description: Recovery codes get you back into an account when you lose your two-factor device. What they are, where to keep them, and what not to do.

item.title: Back up your authenticator before you need to
item.description: If your authenticator lives only on one phone, losing that phone locks you out. How to back up your two-factor codes safely.

item.title: Phishing and fake login pages: how to spot them
item.description: Phishing messages push you to a fake login page that steals your password and code. Warning signs, what to do instead, and where to report it.

item.title: Passkeys vs two-factor codes: what’s the difference?
item.description: Passkeys can’t be typed into a fake website, which makes them stronger than six-digit codes. When to use each, according to FIDO, Google and Apple.

item.title: SIM swapping: how scammers steal your phone number
item.description: In a SIM swap, a scammer moves your phone number to their phone and gets your text message codes. How it works and how to protect yourself.

item.title: Moving to a new phone without losing your codes
item.description: Getting a new phone? Move your two-factor codes over first and keep the old phone until every account works. A step-by-step plan.

item.title: Protect your email first
item.description: Whoever controls your email can reset most of your other passwords. Why your email account deserves your strongest protection, and how.

item.title: Helping your family stay safe online
item.description: Practical ways to help parents, kids and other family members with two-factor login and scams, without taking over their accounts.

item.title: Security tips for travel
item.description: Traveling with your phone and laptop? Keep your two-factor codes working abroad and your accounts safe on public Wi-Fi and charging stations.
